reader.notes: The grammar admits the clauses in any order and the binder processes them order-independently (the PAGE defaults are applied after the loop); AtMostOnce refuses repeats. Five permutations including CODE and GLOBAL produced identical runtime output.

refuter.evidence: Three RD clause orders with all four 1985 clauses (IS GLOBAL, CODE "AB", CONTROL(S) FINAL WS-K, PAGE with HEADING, FIRST DETAIL, LAST DETAIL and FOOTING): sr2x_canon (GLOBAL CODE CONTROL PAGE), sr2x_pcgc (PAGE CODE GLOBAL CONTROL), sr2x_cgpc (CONTROL GLOBAL PAGE CODE). Each also GENERATEs from a contained program through the GLOBAL report. All three exit 0 and write byte-identical report files (md5 aeea8373097b3d35da4595eec6e895bd): the CODE prefix 'AB' is on every line, PH, CF and PF are placed on the right lines, and PAGE-COUNTER goes 01 then 02. So the meaning does not depend on the order, GLOBAL included (X.4.4.2 puts GLOBAL among the clauses after report-name-1). A later edition's form, the 2002 arithmetic-expression SOURCE (pc_rs_source_expr), is refused at 85 with COBOL0900. The reader's duplicate-clause refusals stand. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:XIII.3.5.3 SR2  (3.5.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR2'; 'OK  §1985:X.4.4.4 GR1 ...'.
